newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE taps financial man as new oil minister.
newsitem.headline: UAE taps financial man as new oil minister.

text.p: United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan on Tuesday named a financial man, Obaid bin Saif al-Nasseri, as new oil minister in the OPEC member's first cabinet reshuffle in six years.
Nasseri replaced Rakad bin Salem bin Rakad who had been acting oil minister since June 1995.

The oil-rich Gulf Arab state is a member of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), with an OPEC quota of 2.161 million barrels per day and is one of the few oil producing countries with spare production capacity.

The position of oil minister is not crucial in the UAE, where oil policy is determined by the Supreme Petroleum Council chaired by Sheikh Khalifa bin Zaid al-Nahayan, crown prince of Abu Dhabi and heir apparent to Sheikh Zaid.
Analysts said Nasseri has little experience of the oil industry, but one said "he knows the market and its economics very well".
Industry analysts said the appointment was unlikely to cause a major shift in UAE oil policy. The UAE has traditionally supported moderate world oil prices.

Born in 1952 into a prominent Abu Dhabi family, Nasseri graduated from Baghdad University in 1976 with a BA in economics. Since then, he has been working in the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA). His latest post was director of the commodities department of ADIA.
Nasseri is a member of the Federal National Council, appointed by the rulers, which has a consultative role.
He is also deputy chairman of the UAE Bankers' Association and a member of the board of the National Bank of Abu Dhabi .
The UAE is one of the world's wealthiest countries with oil revenue of $9 billion a year and sufficient crude in the ground to last a century.
